original_question: Given a positive distance d and a plane figure, or more generally a body in space, determine the largest number of points that can be placed in the figure so that every pair of chosen points is at distance at least d. Also determine the smallest set of points {A1, A2, ...} in such a figure with the property that every additional point A in the figure lies within distance d of at least one Ai.
target_in_paper: Unsolved Problem 2(a)-(b): the paper asks for two geometric extremal quantities for a plane figure, and more generally for a body in space—first, the maximum number of points whose pairwise distances are at least d, and second, the minimum number of selected points so that every other point of the figure/body lies at distance < d from one of them. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the correct target almost verbatim: it keeps the two-part structure, the dependence on a positive distance d, the plane-figure / space-body setting, the pairwise-separation condition in part (a), and the covering-by-nearby-chosen-points condition in part (b). ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states explicitly that d>0. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

Part (b) uses the strict inequality AA_i<d; the phrase 'within distance d' can be read as allowing equality, which is not the paper's wording. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, the ambient setting should be stated as a fixed plane figure in the Euclidean plane, or more generally a fixed body in Euclidean 3-space. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
In part (b), the quantified point A is any other point of the same figure/body besides the chosen points {A_i}. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
What is being sought in both parts is an extremal cardinality depending on the given figure/body and on d. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))

The paper adds no further hypotheses such as convexity, regularity, or special shape assumptions, so the refined question should not introduce any. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
refined_question: For a fixed real number d>0 and a fixed plane figure F in the Euclidean plane (or, more generally, a fixed body B in Euclidean 3-space), determine: (a) the largest possible cardinality of a subset S of F (respectively of B) such that |x-y|>=d for every pair of distinct points x,y in S; and (b) the smallest possible cardinality of a subset C={A1,A2,...} of F (respectively of B) such that every point A of F\C (respectively of B\C) satisfies |A-A_i|<d for some A_i in C.
justification: The draft is a near-paraphrase of the paper’s official formulation, so the faithful refinement is to preserve Unsolved Problem 2 exactly rather than broaden it to a more general packing/covering program. The only substantive corrections needed are to make d>0 explicit, restore the strict inequality in part (b), and state the geometric ambient space explicitly enough for the question to stand on its own. This paper is organized as numbered 'Unsolved Problem' statements, and the exact match here is Unsolved Problem 2 on PDF p. 6. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/36UnsolvedProblems.pdf))
